claim: The gut microbiota is implicated in the pathogenesis of hyperuricemia (HUA) and gout.
source: The gut microbiota is implicated in the pathogenesis of hyperuricemia (HUA) and gout.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific understanding.

claim: Lactobacillus plantarum SQ001 was isolated from the cecum of HUA geese.
source: Herein, we isolated Lactobacillus plantarum SQ001 from the cecum of HUA geese and conducted in vitro assays on uric acid (UA) and nucleoside co-culture.
evidence: The manuscript describes the isolation procedure and source of the strain.

claim: L. plantarum SQ001 promotes nucleoside uptake and hydrolysis through its nucleoside hydrolase gene.
source: Metabolomics and genome-wide analyses, revealed that this strain may promote nucleoside uptake and hydrolysis through its nucleoside hydrolase gene.
evidence: Based on metabolomics and genome-wide analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: The functional role of iunH gene was confirmed via heterologous expression and gene knockout studies.
source: The functional role of iunH gene was confirmed via heterologous expression and gene knockout studies.
evidence: The manuscript describes experimental validation through heterologous expression and knockout experiments.

claim: Oral administration of L. plantarum SQ001 resulted in increased abundance of Lactobacillus species and reduced serum UA levels.
source: Oral administration of L. plantarum SQ001 resulted in increased abundance of Lactobacillus species and reduced serum UA levels.
evidence: Based on experimental data from oral gavage studies in geese.

claim: L. plantarum SQ001 downregulated hepatic xanthine oxidase.
source: Furthermore, it downregulated hepatic xanthine oxidase, a key enzyme involved in UA synthesis, as well as renal reabsorption protein GLUT9, while enhancing the expression of renal excretion protein ABCG2.
evidence: Based on experimental measurements of enzyme and protein expression.

claim: L. plantarum SQ001 downregulated renal reabsorption protein GLUT9.

claim: Hyperuricemia (HUA) is a metabolic disorder characterized by elevated serum uric acid (UA) levels exceeding 420 μmol/l (7 mg/dl).
source: Hyperuricemia (HUA) is a metabolic disorder characterized by elevated serum uric acid (UA) levels exceeding 420 μmol/l (7 mg/dl), and affecting 8–25% of the global population (Li et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a definition supported by citation to Li et al., 2022.

claim: HUA affects 8–25% of the global population.
source: Hyperuricemia (HUA) is a metabolic disorder characterized by elevated serum uric acid (UA) levels exceeding 420 μmol/l (7 mg/dl), and affecting 8–25% of the global population (Li et al., 2022).

claim: The incidence of HUA is on the rise, especially among younger populations, driven by diets high in purine and glucose.

claim: HUA has been linked to various health risks including gout, renal injury, diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease.

claim: The regulation of HUA primarily involves three organs: the liver, kidney, and the intestine.
source: The regulation of HUA primarily involves three organs: the liver, kidney, and the intestine (Dalbeth et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Dalbeth et al., 2021.

claim: The upregulation of hepatic purine metabolism and inhibition of renal UA excretion play pivotal roles in the pathogenesis of HUA.
source: The upregulation of hepatic purine metabolism and inhibition of renal UA excretion play pivotal roles in the pathogenesis of HUA, while the intestine contributes to both UA production and excretion (Dalbeth et al., 2021; Niu et al., 2018).
evidence: This mechanistic statement is supported by citations to Dalbeth et al., 2021 and Niu et al., 2018.

claim: The intestine contributes to both UA production and excretion.

claim: The gut accounts for approximately one-third of total urate excretion.
source: The gut accounts for approximately one-third of total urate excretion.

claim: Upon secretion into the gut, UA undergoes metabolism by gut microbes.

claim: Dysbiosis in the gut microbiota is closely associated with dysregulation of urate degradation and systematic inflammation in the host.

claim: Probiotics and prebiotics have emerged as promising natural therapies due to their beneficial effects on gut microbiota regulation and overall health enhancement.

claim: Lactobacillus has been reported to be utilized for modulating the gut microbiota and alleviating HUA.

claim: Geese serve as an excellent model for investigating HUA and gout.
